externalSourceCompleteness.outOfBoundaryNote: All 155 UTM Zone 43N polygons lie within 14 Upper Jhelum / Kashmir Himalayan watersheds.

externalSourceCompleteness.title: CAG of India Report No. 4 of 2025: Conservation and Management of Lakes in Jammu and Kashmir (ended March 2022)
externalSourceCompleteness.outOfBoundaryNote: Jammu Division historical comparison = 367 records (Combined = 697). Official 4-page CAG Press Release retrieved via CloudFront CDN; main saiindia.gov.in timed out (WinError 10060) and cag.gov.in returned HTTP 500, so Appendices 2.1–2.10 (317 remaining individual Kashmir rows: 56 disappeared, 144 decreased, 104 increased, 26 unchanged) remain queued.
externalSourceCompleteness.status: Aggregate Audit Verified + 13 Named Kashmir Lakes Linked; 317 Appendix Rows Queued

externalSourceCompleteness.title: Ministry of Jal Shakti First Census of Water Bodies (2017–18 Reference, All-India & J&K State Report pp. 181–186)
externalSourceCompleteness.outOfBoundaryNote: Of 9,765 enumerated J&K water bodies, only 37 (0.38%) are classified as Lakes; 9,728 are Ponds (5,256), Reservoirs (441), Tanks (179), Check Dams (29), and Others (3,823). Unit-level OGD API CSV requires authenticated key.
externalSourceCompleteness.status: State Annexure Extracted & Strictly Separated from Non-Lake Ponds/Tanks

reconciliationCounts.overlapAdvisory: 78 georeferenced Zenodo glacial lakes (1992–2024) without unambiguous name matches potentially correspond spatially to a subset of ungeoreferenced high-altitude DEERS 2012 tabular tarns (>=3,400 m), and per Section 16 ('Do not force a match where spatial evidence is insufficient') are retained as distinct auditable records until DEERS sheet coordinates are released.
